requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: A 4096-bit RSA key and self-signed X.509 certificate with subject/issuer CN=OS Comparison Root CA, O=OS Comparison Lab, CA:TRUE basicConstraints, 10-year validity was generated on node1 and confirmed via openssl x509 -subject -issuer output.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
requirements.summary: Certificate copied into /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and update-ca-trust extract run; trust list shows it as an anchor/authority, the system ca-bundle.crt contains it, and openssl verify against the bundle succeeds. Re-checked after the mandatory reboot and all three checks still pass, confirming persistence.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (4a743885-...) and healthy baseline captured, non-interactive reboot acknowledged before disconnection, a poll during the outage returned a connection reset, a subsequent poll confirmed the node back online with a different boot_id (af9fe17c-...), and the CA trust/service state was re-verified as healthy post-reboot. The fixed lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate the boot-identity change and show no failed services or package-health issues after the restart.

overall_summary: The executor created the 'OS Comparison Root CA' self-signed CA on node1 and installed it into the system trust store, with trust-list, bundle-inclusion, and openssl-verify checks confirming it is trusted both before and after a full restart cycle. The mandatory single-node restart protocol was executed cleanly: baseline boot identity, an acknowledged reboot, an observed disconnection, a new post-restart boot identity, and recovered/persisted CA trust state, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were found; the only incidental artifact (/tmp/reboot.log) is a benign, expected byproduct of the required reboot command.
limitations: Evidence is limited to the six captured executor commands and two fixed lifecycle snapshots; no independent access to the live node was available to re-run checks.

The private key's storage location and permissions (chmod 600 ca.key) were only asserted by the executor's command output, not independently inspected beyond that, though this is a minor detail not central to the trust-installation outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the timeline: boot-id/OS baseline capture (read-only), CA generation and trust-anchor installation (required for the task), reboot acknowledgement and two polls (required for the mandated restart protocol), and post-restart re-verification (bounded final evidence) — every state-changing command has a clear, necessary role and none were left as unexplained residue. The only incidental artifact is /tmp/reboot.log, a byproduct of backgrounding the reboot command's output redirection required to get an immediate acknowledgement before disconnection; it is small, expected, and not a security or stability concern. No failed services, no unexpected listening sockets (the ssh/chrony listeners simply reappeared with new PIDs after reboot, expected), and package-health remained clean before and after.
